name: Cacao Brown
lede: Cacao brown is the reddish brown of the cacao bean, the seed behind cocoa and chocolate.

sections.title: The bean's brown
sections.body:
Paterson defines cacao brown by the cacao bean, the seed from which cocoa and chocolate are made [1]. The bean is the whole of the definition, with no pigment or date attached [1]. His indexes place it with the browns, near caramel, chocolate and chestnut [2]. Our related names are [[cocoa]], [[chocolate]] and [[caramel]] [3].

The swatch, #AF755E, is a lighter, rosier brown than a roasted bean [3]. Its nearest named color is Terracotta [3].

The dictionary offers no date or origin story for the color name itself [1]. In LCH terms the swatch measures lightness 54, chroma 30 and hue 41 degrees, a moderate chroma for a brown [3]. A screen shows these values only approximately [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this brown in 326 of 23,531 paintings, as photographed [4]. Gilbert Stuart has it in 7 and Pierre-Auguste Renoir in 5 [4]. The count is a computed color match, not an identification of any pigment [4].

questions.q: What does Paterson say cacao brown is the color of?
True or false: the swatch is darker than a roasted bean.

openers: Cacao brown is the color of the bean behind chocolate.
